note.explanation: Renewable energy sources are replaced by new ones after use. Your textbook gives hydroelectricity, solar, wind, tidal, wave and geothermal energy as examples. Non-renewable sources are depleted with continuous use and are not easily replaced once they run out. Fossil fuels and nuclear energy are non-renewable. For example, rain and snowfall replenish water supplies, while fossil fuels take millions of years to form.
examples: Solar energy is renewable because it will remain available.
Fossil fuels are non-renewable because they are limited and take millions of years to form.
note.simple: Renewable sources are replaced after we use them. Non-renewable sources can run out and are not quickly replaced.

note.title: Renewable and Non-Renewable Energy Sources
steps: Check whether the source is replaced after it is used.
If it is replaced, classify it as renewable.
If continuous use depletes it and it is not easily replaced, classify it as non-renewable.
Give examples to support your classification.
note.answer: Renewable sources are replaced by new ones after use; non-renewable sources are depleted with continuous use and are not easily replaced.

written.finalAnswer: Timber or wood can be a renewable source of heat energy if trees are replanted and replaced after use. If trees are cut faster than they grow back, the supply can be depleted.

explain.title: Renewable energy sources
explain.body: “The resources of energy which are replaced by new ones after their use are called renewable energy source.” Examples include hydroelectricity, solar energy, wind energy, tidal energy, wave energy and geothermal energy.

explain.title: Why some sources are renewable
explain.body: Snowfall and rainfall are continuous processes, so water supplies to dam reservoirs are replenished. The textbook also says solar, wind and tidal energy are not going to run out in future.

explain.title: Non-renewable energy sources
explain.body: “non-renewable sources are those, which are depleted with the continuous use. Once they run out, they are not easily replaced by new ones.” Fossil fuels and nuclear energy are examples.

explain.title: Why fossil fuels are limited
explain.body: Fossil fuels formed from the remains of plants and animals buried under the Earth over millions of years. They are limited in quantity, and making new ones takes millions of years.

mistakes: Do not call a source renewable just because it is useful; explain that it is replaced after use.
Do not confuse a source that takes millions of years to form with a renewable source.
Do not list fossil fuels as renewable; the textbook classifies them as non-renewable.
When comparing the two types, give both definitions rather than only giving examples.
Keep examples in the correct category: solar and wind are renewable, while fossil fuels and nuclear energy are non-renewable.
